subject: Live chat: sudden p95/p99 spike during peak — QuickDoc production
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena@quickdoc.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 17 May 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Realtime chat degrading — p99 spikes at 15:00

Hi Grace,

We started seeing severe slowdowns in our live agent chat today around 15:00 PST — messages are taking 6–8s to deliver and some sessions drop with errors. Our users see long typing indicators and a few agents reported timeouts. We load-test at ~600 concurrent websockets during peak; tonight our peak is hitting ~820.

Can your team confirm whether anything changed on the Hosted API side? This is impacting a live support shift.

Attaching a short trace we captured. Please escalate if needed — we need either immediate mitigation or a clear rollback path.

Thanks,
Elena
Customer Success, QuickDoc.ai

Attachment: client-trace-snippet.txt
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@quickdoc.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 17 May 2025 09:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Realtime chat degrading — p99 spikes at 15:00

Hi Elena — thanks for the heads up and for the trace. I'm escalating to infra and the on-call SREs now.

Immediate ask: can you confirm whether the affected sessions were using SSE or WebSocket (I know you use both)? Also any example session ids helps. We'll loop you back with a mitigation plan within 30 minutes.

-G

Grace O'Connor
Director, Customer Success | Redwood Inference
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 17 May 2025 09:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Realtime chat degrading — p99 spikes at 15:00

TL;DR: We see a correlated p95/p99 regression in the streaming host pool (hosted-api-prod-stream-*) beginning 14:55 PST. Error rate up ~3x and p99 latency from ~120ms to ~1.8s for small payloads during bursts.

Details:
- Initial anomaly: sudden queueing on gateway when concurrency >750.
- Likely contributor: batching window heuristics are extending under a spiky concurrency distribution; KV cache hotkey thrashing observed for a subset of model variants (gptx-chat-3b-q4).
- Actions in progress: rolling a conservative batching parameter change to reduce per-request window, and throttling new socket accepts on the overloaded region.

I'm escalating to Exec per Grace's note if we can't guarantee a regression rollback in 45m. Attaching logs + grafana snapshot.

-- Dev
Lead SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachments: sse-tail-logs-20250517.txt, grafana-snapshot-15-00.png
From: Elena Morales <elena@quickdoc.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 17 May 2025 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Realtime chat degrading — p99 spikes at 15:00

Thanks — affected sessions were primarily SSE (about 70%) with fallback to websocket for the rest. Sample session id: qda-conn-9f3c5. We see the errors as 502 gateway errors and occasional 503 throttles.

If you can throttle new connections while you work a fix, that would be best — we'd prefer a small amount of queueing over errors.

-- Elena
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 17 May 2025 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Realtime chat degrading — p99 spikes at 15:00

Update for Exec watch:
- We've applied a temporary reduced-batching rollout (hosts in zone us-west-2b).
- Reasonable improvement in p95 (down ~30%) but p99 still elevated; looks like a small fraction of requests still hitting KV hot paths and suffering long tail.
- We will open a canary that pins to a different model variant (gptx-chat-3b-q2) for high-throughput customers as a fallback; this requires quick approvals for warm-up.

Requesting: Grace, can you confirm whether QuickDoc wants us to failover the entire account to the fallback model or to continue with soft throttles? QuickDoc ops is standing by and prefers throttles if possible.

-Laura
Principal Product Manager, Serving Runtime
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@quickdoc.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 17 May 2025 12:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Realtime chat degrading — p99 spikes at 15:00

Elena — thank you for the quick info and for being patient. We are switching to soft throttles (new-conn backoff) for your account immediately; this will reduce error spikes while Dev and Laura validate the fallback variant.

Next steps (summary for exec):
1) Soft throttles applied to QuickDoc at 12:25 PST — immediate error rate reduction expected.
2) Canary for gptx-chat-3b-q2 starting 12:40 PST; will validate tail behavior over the next 20 minutes.
3) If canary passes, plan a targeted account failover. If it doesn't, we will escalate to a wider rollback of the batching heuristic (risk: slight throughput increase in cost).

Elena — does soft throttling meet your immediate SLA needs for tonight's shift?

Grace
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 17 May 2025 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Realtime chat degrading — p99 spikes at 15:00

Final note for the thread — canary passed at 13:05 PST. p99 dropped from ~1.8s to ~220ms for QuickDoc traffic on the fallback model. Error rate returned to baseline.

We performed a controlled rollback of the aggressive batching heuristic across the affected host pool at 13:30 PST which removed the remaining tail. Cost delta estimated +6% during the window.

Action items:
- Postmortem in draft (internal) — Dev to own.
- Customer-facing summary to Elena by Monday 09:00 PT — Grace to send.
- Investigate KV hotkey mitigations / cache partitioning as medium-term fix — Laura to scope.

Thanks team — we kept QuickDoc live and avoided major outages.

-Aditya
VP, Production Engineering
